justifications.c1: Many independent HMO fire-safety penalties are sourced: Gateshead £42,300, citing a faulty alarm and lack of checks and records (search-confirmed and corroborated by the FIA and The Negotiator); Liverpool £20k; Hatfield agency £50k; and £28k, £13k and £40k cases. Most cover wider failings (an unlicensed HMO, no alarm at all), and enforcement is infrequent per HMO (Wigan: 2 penalties in 2024), so expected loss per site does not show 12-month payback.
justifications.c2: Weekly alarm tests recorded in a logbook are expected by several councils: Cherwell (weekly tests by staff or a competent tenant), Bedford (weekly test by a competent person) and Oxford (BS 5839-6 weekly best practice for Grade A). Great Yarmouth's weekly wording was not seen in search, and the PDPLA disputes that weekly testing is mandatory.
justifications.c3: The manual routine is documented: weekly tests by a manager or tenant, paper logbooks (Merseyside FRS template) and Oxford's annual self-declaration. The only £ figure is a six-monthly service at £153.69 ex VAT (vendor; attribution approximate), and the labour cost of weekly tests was searched for and not found.
justifications.c4: The Management of HMOs (England) Regulations 2006 and s.234 Housing Act 2004 are civil-penalty offences (council policies), and licence conditions require weekly tests and logbooks. Enforcement in this niche is evidenced: Gateshead cites 'lack of safety checks, inspections and records', Liverpool was fined £20k under the Management Regulations over alarm sounders, and Merseyside FRS brought a prosecution. Weekly testing varies by council and is contested.
justifications.c5: Letting and managing agents appear as named defendants (Hatfield, Reading, the £13k and £28k cases), so they plausibly carry the cost. No compliance-manager job title or budget evidence was found, and the landlord base is fragmented.
justifications.c6: Fire-alarm maintainers already visit six-monthly and sell add-on remote monitoring (PLP's ARC connection 'for a small fee'; Protec's cloud subscription built into service plans). Travis Perkins stocks the Aico connected-alarm gateway.
justifications.c7: Willingness to pay is proven, but cheaply: the Aico Ei1000G gateway (about £192 ex VAT, with £60 for 9 years of data per an Aico sheet) covers Grade D RF alarms and reports 'Button Test' events, and C-TEC Envision and Teletek Cloud cover their own panels. The brand-agnostic Grade A gap is only inferred because no such product was found.
justifications.c8: A non-intrusive box reading the sounder and LEDs via microphone and photodiodes is custom sensing that needs per-panel fitting and is prone to false detections. No component prices were found. Mains power and LTE-M are plausible, and Protec notes such cloud links are not life-safety grade.
justifications.c9: There is a recurring record duty: weekly logbook entries for the life of the licence (Cherwell) and annual self-declarations (Oxford). The comparable subscription price is very low, though: Aico at £60 for 9 years (about £0.55/month), and Protec has no stated price.
justifications.c10: Council enforcement releases (Gateshead, Reading, Merseyside FRS) and trade press (FIA, The Negotiator, Landlord Today, Landlords Guild). Forum or first-hand complaints were searched for and not found.

weakest: The comparable incumbent price is tiny (Aico's connected-alarm gateway at about £60 for 9 years of data), and the proposed panel-LED/sounder retrofit is unproven custom sensing with no BOM.
